subject: physics
title: Motion: Speed, Velocity & Acceleration
summary: Speed is a rate — a ratio of distance to time — so this topic reuses ratio/proportion instead of re-teaching it, then extends to velocity, acceleration, and motion graphs.
outcomes: Define speed as a rate (distance per unit time) and compute average speed
Distinguish distance from displacement and speed from velocity (scalar vs vector)
Define acceleration as the rate of change of velocity and compute it
Read and draw distance-time and velocity-time graphs, and interpret their slopes and areas
Apply the equations of uniformly accelerated motion to one-dimensional problems
Convert between m/s and km/h fluently using ratio scaling
